shortDescription: Add or remove MariaDB databases from a remote host

options.name: ca_cert
options.description: The path to a Certificate Authority (CA) certificate. This option, if used, must specify the same certificate as used by the server.

options.name: chdir
options.description: Changes the current working directory. Can be useful, for example, when I(state=import) and a dump file contains relative paths.

options.name: check_hostname
options.description: Whether to validate the server host name when an SSL connection is required. Corresponds to MySQL CLIs C(--ssl) switch. Setting this to C(false) disables hostname verification. Use with caution. Requires pymysql >= 0.7.11.

options.name: check_implicit_admin
options.description: Check if mysql allows login as root/nopassword before trying supplied credentials. If success, passed I(login_user)/I(login_password) will be ignored.

options.name: client_cert
options.description: The path to a client public key certificate.

options.name: client_key
options.description: The path to the client private key.

options.name: collation
options.description: Collation mode (sorting). This only applies to new table/databases and does not update existing ones, this is a limitation of MySQL.

options.name: config_file
options.description: Specify a config file from which user and password are to be read. The default config file, C(~/.my.cnf), if it exists, will be read, even if I(config_file) is not specified. The default config file, C(~/.my.cnf), if it exists, must contain a C([client]) section as a MySQL connector requirement. To prevent the default config file from being read, set I(config_file) to be an empty string.

options.name: config_overrides_defaults
options.description: If C(yes), connection parameters from I(config_file) will override the default values of I(login_host) and I(login_port) parameters. Used when I(stat) is C(present) or C(absent), ignored otherwise. It needs Python 3.5+ as the default interpreter on a target host.

options.name: connect_timeout
options.description: The connection timeout when connecting to the MySQL server.

options.name: dump_extra_args
options.description: Provide additional arguments for mysqldump. Used when I(state=dump) only, ignored otherwise.

options.name: encoding
options.description: Encoding mode to use, examples include C(utf8) or C(latin1_swedish_ci), at creation of database, dump or importation of sql script.

options.name: force
options.description: Continue dump or import even if we get an SQL error. Used only when I(state) is C(dump) or C(import).

options.name: hex_blob
options.description: Dump binary columns using hexadecimal notation.

options.name: ignore_tables
options.description: A list of table names that will be ignored in the dump of the form database_name.table_name.

options.name: login_host
options.description: Host running the database. In some cases for local connections the I(login_unix_socket=/path/to/mysqld/socket), that is usually C(/var/run/mysqld/mysqld.sock), needs to be used instead of I(login_host=localhost).

options.name: login_password
options.description: The password used to authenticate with.

options.name: login_port
options.description: Port of the MySQL server. Requires I(login_host) be defined as other than localhost if login_port is used.

options.name: login_unix_socket
options.description: The path to a Unix domain socket for local connections. Use this parameter to avoid the C(Please explicitly state intended protocol) error.

options.name: login_user
options.description: The username used to authenticate with.

options.name: master_data
options.description: Option to dump a master replication server to produce a dump file that can be used to set up another server as a slave of the master. C(0) to not include master data. C(1) to generate a 'CHANGE MASTER TO' statement required on the slave to start the replication process. C(2) to generate a commented 'CHANGE MASTER TO'. Can be used when I(state=dump).

options.name: name
options.description: Name of the database to add or remove. I(name=all) may only be provided if I(state) is C(dump) or C(import). List of databases is provided with I(state=dump), I(state=present) and I(state=absent). If I(name=all) it works like --all-databases option for mysqldump (Added in 2.0).

options.name: pipefail
options.description: Use C(bash) instead of C(sh) and add C(-o pipefail) to catch errors from the mysql_dump command when I(state=dump) and compression is used.

options.name: quick
options.description: Option used for dumping large tables.

options.name: restrict_config_file
options.description: Read only passed I(config_file). When I(state) is C(dump) or C(import), by default the module passes I(config_file) parameter using C(--defaults-extra-file) command-line argument to C(mysql/mysqldump) utilities under the hood that read named option file in addition to usual option files. If this behavior is undesirable, use C(yes) to read only named option file.

options.name: single_transaction
options.description: Execute the dump in a single transaction.

options.name: skip_lock_tables
options.description: Skip locking tables for read. Used when I(state=dump), ignored otherwise.

options.name: sql_log_bin
options.description: Whether binary logging should be enabled or disabled for the connection.

options.name: state
options.description: The database state.

options.name: target
options.description: Location, on the remote host, of the dump file to read from or write to. Uncompressed SQL files (C(.sql)) as well as bzip2 (C(.bz2)), gzip (C(.gz)), xz (Added in 2.0) and zstd (C(.zst)) (Added in 3.12.0) compressed files are supported.

options.name: unsafe_login_password
options.description: If C(no), the module will safely use a shell-escaped version of the I(login_password) value. It makes sense to use C(yes) only if there are special symbols in the value and errors C(Access denied) occur. Used only when I(state) is C(import) or C(dump) and I(login_password) is passed, ignored otherwise.

options.name: use_shell
options.description: Used to prevent C(Broken pipe) errors when the imported I(target) file is compressed. If C(yes), the module will internally execute commands via a shell. Used when I(state=import), ignored otherwise.
